title: Excel on the web: Copilot Agent Mode (Edit with Copilot) builds and edits workbooks through chat
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licence requirement and documented controls are supported. Clarify Microsoft's differing descriptions of the EU/EFTA and UK Claude defaults, and extend the DLP route beyond selecting the policy location.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot performs multi-step workbook updates on the user's request.
claims.quote: Saves you time by letting Copilot perform multi-step workbook updates while you stay focused on insights.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot works in the user's workbook within the user's content-access permissions.
claims.quote: All Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the security context of the user who initiates the prompt. This means for a user to see an item in a prompt response, they must first have the necessary permissions to access the content of the item.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[2].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork DLP location can exclude sensitivity-labelled files from Copilot processing, including in Excel.
claims.quote: This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Opening an Excel file with a sensitivity label covered by a prevent-processing DLP policy disables Copilot skills in the app.
claims.quote: When a file is open in Word, Excel, or PowerPoint and has a sensitivity label for which DLP policy is configured to prevent processing by Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat, the skills in these apps are disabled.

claims.claim: The prevent-processing policy is evaluated at file open in Excel.
claims.quote: In Word, Excel, and PowerPoint the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy to prevent Copilot from processing content is evaluated at file open.

claims.claim: A sensitivity label applied mid-session is enforced the next time the file is opened.
claims.quote: If a sensitivity label is applied mid-session, the policy will be enforced starting the next time the file is opened.

claims.claim: Claude models in these experiences are excluded from in-country processing commitments where applicable.
claims.quote: currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary, and when applicable, in-country processing commitments.

claims.claim: Managing the Anthropic setting requires AI Administrator or Global Administrator.

claims.claim: No change to sign-in or permissions is documented for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: "Edit with Copilot" "Excel" "sign-in" "permissions"; read release-notes entry 527835, Business Central across-work-with-excel and Purview DLP coverage. No feature-specific change to sign-in or permissions was stated.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Important Anthropic setting changes for EU, EFTA and UK tenants take effect on December 9, 2026.
claims.quote: On December 9, 2026, there are important changes taking effect to this setting.

claims.claim: The service description publishes no separate charge or meter for Edit with Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: "Edit with Copilot" "meter" "price"; read the entire Microsoft Copilot service description and the Copilot pay-as-you-go meters search excerpt. The service description names the add-on entitlement but no separate Edit with Copilot charge or meter.

claims.claim: The service description says Microsoft Purview controls for Copilot require a Microsoft Purview licence.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview controls: Requires license for Microsoft Purview, available as part of Microsoft 365 G3/G5 or as a standalone.

claims.claim: The service description shows Edit with Copilot as not currently available in GCC, GCCH and DoD.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote: GCC Not currently available; GCCH Not currently available; DoD Not currently available.

claims.claim: Structured Excel data analysis is affected in government clouds until Edit with Copilot in Excel is released there.
claims.quote: Copilot's ability to analyze structured Excel data is impacted until Edit with Copilot in Excel is released in GCC, GCC-High and DoD.

claims.claim: Claude models are enabled by default for most commercial customers.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Claude models on by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).

claims.claim: Claude models are disabled by default for customers within the EU Data Boundary and in the UK.
claims.quote: Customers within the EU Data Boundary and customers in the UK have Claude models disabled by default. The linked apps-only page also states: This setting is enabled by default for tenants in the EU, EFTA, and UK that were created after March 25, 2026.
claims.fix: Keep the cited general default but add: 'Microsoft's apps-only guidance separately says the All users for Microsoft 365 apps only option is enabled by default for EU/EFTA and UK tenants created after March 25, 2026; administrators of older tenants should check their setting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/copilot-anthropic-apps. This reports both Microsoft descriptions rather than implying the general default settles every Excel tenant's setting.

claims.claim: Claude models are unavailable to federal GCC customers and all GCC High and DoD customers.
claims.quote: Claude models aren't available for federal customers in GCC or for any customers in GCC High and Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: Anthropic user and group assignments apply at provider level across Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences.
claims.quote: These assignments are applied at the provider level and enforced across Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The licence control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user ... In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses containing SkuId, and RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[1].ui; rendered controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The printed Microsoft 365 admin center route reaches Anthropic user and group access selection.
claims.quote: Copilot > Settings > View all ... AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors ... Available subprocessors for your organization ... Anthropic ... Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences

claims.claim: No automation operation is documented for the Anthropic provider user and group access setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors Graph API PowerShell settings; Anthropic Graph subprocessor API; admin-settings Anthropic ai provider API. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor, copilotPolicySetting and returned apps-only excerpts; no operation for this setting.

claims.claim: The printed Purview route reaches the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location when creating a custom DLP policy.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: The path stops at selecting the location, before configuring the rule. Extend it to 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels'. Keep the note naming the rule action 'Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPComplianceRule call creates a Copilot DLP rule with an advanced label condition and ExcludeContentProcessing set to Block.
claims.quote: New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The rule uses Content contains > Sensitivity labels and Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content.
claims.quote: Content contains > Sensitivity labels | Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content | Detects when a file or an email in Exchange has a chosen sensitivity label.

claims.quote: Searched: Edit with Copilot Excel disable turn off admin setting Agent Mode Graph policy; Excel Edit with Copilot admin disable. claims.claim: The Graph copilotPolicySetting reference lists Block Copilot Access to Open Content as a Cloud Policy setting.
claims.quote: Represents a Copilot setting that is managed through a policy service (CPS or Intune). microsoft.copilot.blockaccesstoopenfiles | Block Copilot Access to Open Content
